title: Grade 5 French — Tue, Jun 24
description: Les métiers — Day 2 of 5: Feminine forms of professions
subject: french

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'un acteur' (an actor)?
questions.explanation: 'Un acteur' (m) → 'une actrice' (f). This is an irregular feminine — not simply adding 'e'. Compare: directeur→directrice, instituteur→institutrice.

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'un chanteur' (a singer)?
questions.explanation: 'Un chanteur' → 'une chanteuse'. The -eur suffix changes to -euse for the feminine in many professions: danseur→danseuse, vendeur→vendeuse.

questions.question: 'Un professeur' in French is unusual because:
options: The word itself stays 'professeur' for both genders in traditional use — though 'une professeure' is increasingly used in modern French
All professions are the same for male and female
questions.explanation: Traditionally 'professeur' was invariable (same for male/female). Modern French increasingly uses 'une professeure' or 'une prof' (informal). Language evolves!

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'un médecin' (a doctor)?
options: une médecin (increasingly: une médecine or simply une médecin)
questions.explanation: 'Médecin' was traditionally invariable. Modern usage: 'une médecin' (most common) or 'une femme médecin'. 'Doctoresse' exists but is old-fashioned. In practice: 'Elle est médecin.'

questions.question: What is the feminine of 'un cuisinier'?
questions.explanation: 'Un cuisinier' → 'une cuisinière'. The -ier suffix becomes -ière in the feminine: boulanger→boulangère, épicier→épicière.

questions.question: Translate: 'She is an engineer.'
questions.explanation: 'Elle est ingénieure.' ✓ Modern French adds -e for feminine: ingénieur→ingénieure. No article needed after être in professions.

questions.question: What is the feminine of 'un danseur' (a dancer)?
Identify the correct feminine: 'She is an actress.'
questions.explanation: 'Elle est actrice.' ✓ Profession after être = no article. Actrice is the feminine of acteur.

questions.question: What is the general rule for professions ending in '-eur'?
questions.explanation: Most -eur professions → -euse: chanteur/chanteuse, danseur/danseuse, vendeur/vendeuse. Exception: -teur often → -trice: acteur/actrice, directeur/directrice.

questions.question: What is the feminine of 'un agriculteur' (a farmer)?
questions.explanation: 'Un agriculteur' → 'une agricultrice'. Pattern -teur → -trice: directeur/directrice, instituteur/institutrice, agriculteur/agricultrice.

questions.question: Some professions are the same for both genders. Which from this list is invariable?
questions.explanation: 'Architecte' is invariable — 'un architecte' (male) and 'une architecte' (female). Same form, different article. Other invariable: médecin, professeur (traditionally), juge, ministre.

questions.question: In French, why does the language have evolving feminine forms for professions?
options: As more women entered all professions, French evolved to reflect reality — using feminine forms acknowledges that women hold these roles
It was always the rule — nothing changed
questions.explanation: Historically, many professions were male-dominated and had no feminine forms. As women entered all fields, French (like all living languages) adapted. Official bodies now recommend feminine forms: auteure, professeure, ingénieure.

questions.question: Spot the error: 'Ma mère est une chanteuse professionnel.'
options: 'professionnel' should be 'professionnelle' — adjectives must agree with the noun (chanteuse is feminine → professionnelle)
questions.explanation: 'Chanteuse' is feminine → adjective must also be feminine: 'professionnelle' (not 'professionnel'). Correct: 'Ma mère est une chanteuse professionnelle.'

questions.question: What is the feminine of 'un directeur'?
questions.explanation: 'Un directeur' → 'une directrice'. Pattern: -teur → -trice. Common in professions: directeur/directrice, instructeur/instructrice, réalisateur/réalisatrice.

questions.question: Write a sentence: 'My sister is a firefighter.' in French.
questions.explanation: 'Ma sœur est pompière.' ✓ 'Pompier' → 'pompière' (feminine: adds -ière). Profession after être = no article. 'Ma sœur' = my sister.
